newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - NeXstar aims for '97 profitability.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - NeXstar aims for '97 profitability.

text.p: The U.S. approval of NeXstar Pharmaceuticals Inc's AmBisome antifungal and increased sales of its DaunoXome anticancer drug are key to driving the company into the black in 1997, its Chief Executive Patrick Mahaffy said on Tuesday.
"Those are the two events that can give us that sales level that can sustain us in profitability," Mahaffy said in an interview.
Industry analysts expect the Boulder, Colo.-based biotechnology company to earn $0.54 a share in 1997, according to First Call, compared to a previously predicted loss of $0.30 in 1996.
Last month NeXstar's U.S. marketing and development patrner Fujisawa USA Inc, a unit of Japan's Fujisawa Pharmaceutical Co Ltd, filed for U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval of AmBisome.
"We're hopeful to get a 1997 approval," Mahaffy said.
He said he expects the drug to have non-U.S. sales of about $75-$80 million in 1996, up from $56 million in 1995.
